gaps.sentence: "You broke my phone!" — She accused me ___ her phone.
'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'How much does this cost?' I asked the vendor. I asked the vendor how much it ___.
gaps.explanation: does cost → cost: the past simple of 'cost' is 'cost', used with statement word order.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
"Do not touch the wire!" — She warned me ___ the wire.
gaps.explanation: 'Warn somebody not to do' — 'not' comes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.
